long_biography.plain_text:
Property development became part of Remon Fayad's working life early. He spent school holidays on building sites and joined his father after leaving school, learning the business from project conception to delivery. Planning and land acquisition became his specialities, and he later held development-director and chief-operating roles while helping assemble multi-building apartment projects around Sydney.

With his brother, Fayad developed an agency model that separated site ownership from delivery. Family investors bought the land, while the agency coordinated planning, design, construction oversight, sales, leasing and ongoing management; it could offer the same services to third-party landowners. This structure was intended to retain responsibility beyond an apartment sale and to support residential, retail, office and public-space components within a single precinct.

Terminal resolved-person dossier. The existing yacht-led biography is replaced with durable, source-hidden property-career prose. Real Estate is supported by sustained development leadership, Ellerson ownership and a court-identified property economic interest; it is not inferred from employment alone. The family-transfer origin follows the strict succession test at medium confidence: an established family property platform, succession into owner-operator roles, family-owned project land and personal economic interest are all evidenced, but no inheritance or precise transfer instrument is claimed. Current wealth relationship is Unknown because Operator is historical, the main businesses entered administration or ceased ABN registration and Fayad was made bankrupt in July 2025. The active sole-trader ABN does not reveal a sector or principal asset. No research has been compiled or applied.

[3] Property developer: His long-term work in acquisition, planning, executive operations and development-agency ownership satisfies the occupation contract as former but defining. [5] Residential development: Apartment towers were central to the career, but the broad tag is omitted in favour of the more specific mixed-use cohort under consolidation rules. [6] Family property interests: Court reasons identify an ultimate economic interest through intermediary companies before bankruptcy; the evidence supports the wealth mechanism and family-transfer inference but not a current tag.
